sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises sharply once utilization passes about 72% of the credit limit.
The number of past delinquencies is the second or third most important driver, and risk mostly increases with it, mainly moving from zero to one or more.
Annual income is also among the top three drivers, and higher income is associated with lower risk, though the effect is moderate and its shape is less clear.
Length of credit history has a weak effect, with longer histories associated with somewhat lower risk.
The data do not settle whether debt-to-income ratio matters at all at this sample size.
The remaining features, including the two application attributes, age and recent credit inquiries, have effects that hardly matter.
Utilization's effect is stronger for applicants with more past delinquencies, while the other interactions are small and do not change the picture.
